newsitem.title: DUBAI: Disabled Iran veterans protest at German mission.
newsitem.headline: Disabled Iran veterans protest at German mission.

text.p: About 200 Iranian veterans disabled in Iraqi chemical attacks prepared on Thursday to spend their second night outside the German embassy in Tehran in protest against a verdict accusing Iran of ordering political killings, witnesses said.

Witnesses said the protesters set up tents across the street from the mission for the sit-in which was also held to back demands to bring to justice German firms accused of supplying toxic chemicals to Baghdad during the 1980-88 Iran-Iraq war.

The demonstrators had been among thousands who had marched to the embassy on Wednesday in the fourth demonstration at the barricaded mission after the court accused Iranian leaders of ordering the 1992 killings of four Kurdish dissidents in Berlin.
Iran has repeatedly denied any role in the slayings, which it blames on infighting between opposition groups.

Gruesome pictures of victims of chemical arms had been posted in front of the embassy by the protesters, some of whom had left hospitals to attend the sit-in. They were cared for at a makeshift clinic set by authorities at the protest site.
Iran has said court proceedings would begin shortly against 24 German companies accused of having helped Iraq produce chemical weapons during the war.
State-run Tehran radio earlier carried reports from protest marches against the verdict, which were held on Thursday in half a dozen cities across Iran.
The German ruling issued last Thursday sparked a diplomatic row between Iran and Germany, until recently Tehran's main trade partner and most important Western friend.
Iran has responded to the recalling for consultations of all European Union ambassadors, except Greece's, by announcing it would reciprocate.
